A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Bi-LoRA research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable, and relocated or renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model and diffusion-model experiments, efficiency measurements, sensitivity analyses, and quantized fine-tuning results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds Qwen experiments, broader comparisons, component ablations, and adversarial parameter-perturbation tests.

M1.justification: Equations (7)–(10) and Algorithm 1 retain the same dual-adapter objective, simultaneous descent/ascent updates, global Frobenius-norm clipping, and removal of the auxiliary adapter at inference. New theoretical interpretations and ablation variants do not change the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: The training datasets, evaluation benchmarks, and task requirements are retained. Qwen uses the existing Cleaned Alpaca/INSTRUCTEVAL pipeline. The added CoLA weight-perturbation analysis changes the model-testing procedure, without introducing new data populations or input conditions.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds random-output and random-weight perturbation baselines, LoRA-ESAM, and LoRA-LookSAM, and extends BAR/Flat-LoRA comparisons to retained chat and instruction tasks. Appendix H adds HiRA, DeLoRA, WSAM, and S2-SAM comparisons, and evaluates PiSSA and DoRA on Llama instruction tasks beyond their existing T5 comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds the Qwen 2.5-14B configuration and component-control, attack, and expanded sensitivity protocols. Existing settings also change: Llama 2 micro-batches become 4 for all three tasks instead of 2/1/1, and its reported Bi-LoRA radius changes from 0.1 to 0.05 (v1 Appendix H.2 versus v2 Appendix R.2). These documented revisions do not establish that every retained result was rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses isolate adversarial ascent versus extra adapter capacity and compare global, per-layer, and absent clipping (Table 5). v2 also adds Llama learning-rate and joint rank/radius sensitivity studies, adversarial parameter robustness (Appendix N), and a LoRA-SAM rank sweep (Appendix U). Earlier T5 sensitivity, convergence, quantization, and generalization-gap analyses remain.

E5.justification: v2 Table 3 adds uncertainty to aggregate SDXL CLIP scores and specifies 200 runs for each of six prompt instances; v1 reported per-instance point estimates and described 200 prompts. The general three-run standard-error convention and special NLU run counts remain unchanged. The revised SDXL description does not establish an increase in independent training runs.

E6.justification: Substantial Qwen, baseline, ablation, robustness, and rank-sweep results are added. Existing values also change: Flat-LoRA's GSM8K score changes from 60.65 in v1 Table 5 to 59.44 in v2 Table 1, while Bi-LoRA remains 60.32. MT-Bench and timing values are revised. Per-instance SDXL scores and T5/Llama 2 peak-memory entries disappear; NLU accuracy results are retained. Revised settings limit direct performance comparisons.

T1.justification: v2 introduces Propositions 2 and 3 and Appendix F proofs concerning ascent-gradient alignment and an idealized Ky Fan gradient-norm regularizer, plus Appendix V's mathematical comparison with other methods. Earlier subspace reasoning remains, including the former Proposition 4.1 in prose. These are substantial formal additions, although Equation (A18) violates the stated Frobenius constraint for rank greater than one.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: an auxiliary adversarial adapter decouples perturbation from adaptation, permits one backward pass, broadens sharpness exploration, and improves generalization efficiently. Reordering the efficiency and subspace arguments does not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations attributing gains to adversarial ascent rather than additional capacity, motivating global clipping, and invoking continuity between successive gradients. It acknowledges a gap between ideal inner optimization and practical single-step updates. However, v1's explicit limitations paragraph is removed, while Appendix V newly asserts inherited SAM generalization and convergence guarantees.

D1.justification: v2 adds a Bi-LoRA repository link, a reproducibility statement, Qwen hyperparameter/search settings, and settings for new baselines. Most existing implementation documentation remains. Hardware assignments are revised, but Appendix P's A100 allocation for LLM experiments conflicts with Appendix S's retained statement that all timing experiments use an RTX 4090.

R1.justification: Beyond relocating the existing survey to Appendix E, v2 substantially expands its positioning through SAM convergence and regularization theory, low-rank gradient arguments, and Appendix V's formal comparison with BAR and Flat-LoRA. New references include relevant theory and additional LoRA methods. Flat-LoRA's workshop-to-ICML citation update represents the same work, not a newly introduced comparator.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten to foreground computational efficiency. Related work and NLU experiments move to appendices, the main experimental narrative centers on larger models, and the appendix structure expands and reorganizes substantially. These changes exceed local wording edits.

P2.justification: v2 expands and consolidates comparison tables, adds Qwen and ablation tables and sensitivity heatmaps, replaces the per-instance diffusion table with aggregates, and redistributes NLU displays. A previously appended convergence panel and existing SDXL examples are redisplayed in the main text; these are presentation changes rather than wholly new experimental evidence.

improvement.justification: Broader comparisons, larger-model evaluation, and component and robustness controls substantially strengthen v1's empirical case. However, the new regularizer proof uses rho times U_r V_r transpose, whose Frobenius norm is rho times sqrt(r), violating its own bound and undermining Proposition 3. The new SST2 column in Table A4 also repeats 60.15 ± 0.36 at every radius. These reliability problems, alongside stronger theoretical assertions and removed limitations, make the net quality effect uncertain despite the empirical improvements.
